fail_reasons: security 4 < 7 (critical tier auto-fail). The two families the 40th verdict measured ARE closed (27 of 29 cells flipped allow→ask; differential measured against 8e411f9, which allows all 29). But lab-confirmed live control-plane destruction still reaches `allow` through a THIRD family on the very axis this round was chartered to close — case-varied `.claude` whose target is reached through the `rest` tail: `find .CLAUDE/PLUGINS -delete`, `find .Claude/Plugins -delete`, `find .CLAUDE/plugins -delete`, `find .CLAUDE/plugins/myplug -delete`, `mv .CLAUDE/plugins /tmp/sink`, `bash -c "find .CLAUDE/plugins -delete"` — all allow, and in a fresh mktemp lab all six deleted `.claude/plugins/**` (the installed-plugin tree, i.e. where this harness's own hooks live). Canonical `find .claude/plugins -delete` is ask, so this is a notation/comparison leak, not declared scope. Root cause is one line: `rest=${t##*.claude/}` (hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:1533) is a PARAMETER EXPANSION, and bash's `nocasematch` governs only `case`, `[[ … == … ]]` and `=~` — never parameter-expansion patterns. Verified directly: with `shopt -s nocasematch`, `t='.CLAUDE/PLUGINS'; rest=${t##*.claude/}` yields `.CLAUDE/PLUGINS` unchanged, so the `plugins)` / `plugins/*)` arms miss. The sibling `hooks` arm survives ONLY by accident of its wildcard spelling (`hooks|*/hooks` happens to match the unstripped `.CLAUDE/HOOKS`), and `hooks/*.sh` likewise — which is why `find .CLAUDE/hooks -delete` is ask while `find .CLAUDE/plugins -delete` is allow.

Criterion: for every arm of `__control_plane_location_impl`, the generated suite emits at least one target that reaches that arm, crossed with the full notation × case product.

A criterion is needed that the comparison-semantics rule holds for EVERY construct that inspects a control-plane name, not every `case` statement — naming parameter expansion (`${t##…}`, `${t%…}`, `${t#…}`), `[[ -f … ]]`/`[[ -d … ]]` filesystem probes, and plain string equality as constructs that `shopt` does not reach. The two anchoring strategies need a stated symmetry requirement: judgment (b) anchors `.claude` by name and judgment (c) anchors `hooks` by filesystem reality, and any spelling the guard cannot resolve (an unexpanded `$PWD`, a parameter, a substitution) silently defeats only the reality-anchored one. f65_residual_judgment.sc10_7_status: Formally satisfied for this axis as of this commit — the key exists, names the six forms, states the severity, and retracts the false in-code comment. The registration is honest and well written.
f65_residual_judgment.judgment: This residual alone is sufficient to withhold pass, independently of the two new leak families. F65's contract is that control-plane destruction does not execute without a prompt; `find .claude -exec rm -rf {} +` is not an exotic spelling but the standard portable idiom for exactly that deletion, it is one token away from `find .claude -delete` which IS gated, and it executes silently. SC-10(7) requires allow cells to be attributed, not that attribution makes them acceptable — attribution is a bookkeeping control that prevents quiet scope loss, and reading it as a pass-gate would let any leak be converted into a pass by writing a ledger entry. The implementer was right not to close it inside step 16's approved scope and right to register it; the correct next move is a `/change-request` for the `find` predicate axis as a whole (`-exec`, `-execdir`, `-ok`, and interpreters invoked behind them), with its own Plan gate. Until that axis is closed, security cannot reach 7 for a critical-tier feature.
f65_residual_judgment.recommendation: Open a change-request for the find-predicate axis. Treat it as the successor to this round rather than as part of it, and keep it out of any round whose scope is notation or comparison semantics.
